_comment: Worked example extract for the workload-model engine (SCOPE stage). These are the telemetry-derived facts of a CrewAI + DeepSeek agent app observed over one clean, deploy-free load window — the behavioral split comes from whether a turn invokes a tool (ReAct loop) or stays pure-LLM. This file is the generic `extract.json` contract the engine consumes; see docs/engine.md. Run: `workload-engine --extract examples/crewai-deepseek-agent/extract.json --out out --mode agentic` (exit 0 iff the G0 gate passes). Every field below was derived from server spans over the window; no production PII.
name: crewai-deepseek-agent
timeframeNotes: single-service agent app; entry scoped to the agent service, co-tenant services dropped by scope
queries: fetch spans | filter is_root_span && service.name=='crewai-deepseek-agent' | summarize count() by entryOp  (front-end discovery -> single entry request)
fetch logs | filter k8s.container.name=='istio-proxy' over window -> 0 lines  (access-log probe, spans-only)
fetch spans | join [spans|sort start_time asc|summarize collectArray(span.name) by trace.id] on trace.id  (JOURNEY reconstruction: ReAct loop vs single LLM round)
fetch spans | summarize countIf(span.name=='execute_tool') by trace.id | summarize count() by usesTool  (archetype split via tool-use terminal signal)
fetch spans | filter span.name=='agent.turn' | summarize percentile(duration,50/95/99),avg by usesTool  (per-archetype baseline)
fetch spans | filter request | summarize count() by bin(start_time,1m)  (G3-B arrival curve; interior CoV 0.016 -> steady)
fetch spans | filter span.name=='agent.turn' | summarize sum(duration) / window  (observed concurrency)

arrival._note: observedConcurrency = busy-time integral sum(agent.turn duration)/window; meanServerResponseMs is the server span, not the load-driver wrapper

archetypes.name: Conversational — pure-LLM turn (single round); no tool
archetypes.description: Conversational — pure-LLM turn (single round); no tool. Reconstructed flow: request -> agent.turn -> llm.call -> chat -> finalize -> message.sent

archetypes.name: Agentic — tool-using turn (ReAct: LLM -> tool -> LLM); reaches execute_tool
archetypes.description: Agentic — tool-using turn (ReAct: LLM -> tool -> LLM). Reconstructed flow: request -> agent.turn -> llm.call -> chat -> execute_tool(web_search|calculator) -> llm.call -> chat -> finalize -> message.sent

fields.name: task
values: search the web for the latest OTel release and summarize
calculate the 95th percentile of these latencies

fields.name: task
values: explain distributed tracing in one paragraph

exclusions: none within service scope — all entry traces are application traffic
targetEnv: non-production agent-demo namespace (production forbidden without explicit approval)
abortNote: Abort ABOVE the agentic tail: tool-using turns reach p99 35061 ms (ReAct + 2nd LLM round) vs conversational p99 16350 ms — set p95 abort > 8000 ms, errorRate abort 5%.
risks: **Behavioral split via a terminal-action signal.** Archetypes are distinguished by whether the flow reaches a tool-invocation span (ReAct) vs stays pure-LLM — the same agnostic classifier the commerce example uses with an order-terminal signal (payment/checkout).

**Arrival is STEADY.** The driver is constant-arrival-rate; the interior per-minute CoV is 0.016, so the model emits one steady stage + a mandatory ramp-down tail (R2: still mean arrival, no production diurnal envelope).

**Tool-using turns are ~2.3x heavier** (mean 3714 ms vs 1611 ms) — modeled as separate baselines so a load test exercises both the cheap conversational path and the expensive ReAct path at their true ~32/68 mix.

provenance.note: Worked example (sanitized demo of a real demo-tenant extraction): tenant anonymized to 'agent-demo' and fields normalized to the engine contract. Treat as demo data: consumers require explicit --demo opt-in (ISI-5928).
